messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>

Subject: Planned US-West runtime safety window — Jun 12-13 (staged restarts)

Hi all,

We're scheduling a staged runtime safety window for our US-West region to deploy updated kernel/driver bundles and a small runtime hotfix. This is a planned maintenance event to address recent driver edge cases that can cause rare inference stalls under long-token sessions.

Window (staged across pools):
- Start: Sat, Jun 12 2026 at 02:00 PDT
- End: Sun, Jun 13 2026 at 08:00 PDT

What to expect:
- Rolling restarts of node pools over ~30 hours; we will do small batches to preserve capacity.
- Short-lived token-generation interruptions for in-flight requests on affected nodes (typically < 6s) while KV caches are rehydrated.
- No model version changes. Models and routing remain the same.

Impact level: low (best-effort continuity). For most customers there will be no user-visible degradation; a subset of long-running streaming sessions or very large-batch synchronous calls might see a single short stall or a reconnect.

Mitigations and options for customers:
1) We will run canary pools early in the window. If you'd like your traffic routed through the canary (for earlier validation), reply to this thread and we can add your account to the canary cohort.
2) If you run long-lived streaming sessions, consider: smaller streaming chunks or client-side reconnect logic during the window.
3) We will enable automatic fallback to a compatible model variant in other regions for critical traffic if requested (this will require an allowlist).

Operational details and attachments:
- Attached: us-west-maintenance-playbook.pdf (runbook, rollback steps) and impact-matrix-usw.csv (service-by-service impact and schedule).
- Live status updates will be posted to: https://status.redwood.example.com/maintenance/us-west-2026-06
- HubSpot maintenance record: HS-98742

Internal notes: Monica/Marcus, please publish the status page banner and queue CS runbooks; Laura, please coordinate with Dedicated ops to ensure reserved pools are excluded unless explicitly opted in.

I'll post a short pre-window reminder 48 hours before the start.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Ops Manager — Runtime Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: (2) us-west-maintenance-playbook.pdf (application/pdf), impact-matrix-usw.csv (text/csv)

Hi Sam — thanks for the quick questions, answers below: 

1) Canary cohort: yes — we've reserved a small canary slot for partners/customers who opt in. To enroll, reply here with the test key (or send it to me off-thread) and we'll route a copy of your production-like traffic through the canary pool starting Jun 12 02:30 PDT. Marcus will share canary validation metrics by 04:30 PDT each day.

2) Opt-out impact: opting out will not prevent you from being updated later; however, delaying places you into the normal rotation which may be scheduled after the canary validation. There is a small risk (low probability) of an emergency hotpatch if we observe a post-window regression — in that case we'd coordinate directly, but we generally avoid urgent forced upgrades unless the issue is severity-high. If you require hardened timing SLAs, we can discuss a Dedicated pool exemption with a targeted upgrade plan.

3) Evidence / artifacts: driver bundles, checksums, and the minimal changelog are attached in the playbook under /artifacts. I'll also upload SHA256 artifacts to our internal artifacts bucket and provide signed links to your security team. Example: https://status.redwood.example.com/maintenance/us-west-2026-06/artifacts (read-only, expiring link).

Next steps:
- Marcus: add Acme (sam.ross@acme-retail.com) to canary cohort and confirm the test key route.
- Monica: ensure CS is prepared for opt-in and opt-out handling.
- Sam: send the test key (or indicate you want us to generate one).

I'll follow up with a 48-hour reminder that includes the exact per-pool schedule and a lightweight runbook snippet for customer engineers.

Best,
Diego
